approach: Fix the class at its two origins, and define "no process" by the same signal the codebase already uses for liveness (registry entry OR held job lock). (A) Origin in the run: `Athena::dispatch` commits the job record and brief (run/mod.rs:1249-1257); every later `?` (plan_round 1314, produce_and_verify 1335/1762) returns Err with no outcome, and `RealSteps::run` maps that to `Run{outcome: None}` (drain.rs:4395-4408). Wrap the post-commit part of `dispatch`: an error that is not a deliberate hold (LowDisk, SlotWait, BudgetShort), with the kill switch off and no resume mark, closes the job `failed` with a stated reason through the existing `close_dispatched`, booking only the invocations that actually left a trace (new `recover_traces`, no synthesized producer). (B) Origin in the listing: `steward::interrupted_work` keeps only the cli/steward channels (steward.rs:467) and hides every job any later request retries (448-460), whatever became of that retry. Drop the channel filter for interrupted jobs only, reuse `retries_by_job` (a dropped retry does not stand), take liveness from a new `Athena::in_flight(job)` (registry entry or job lock held; status.rs), and add a pure `steward::settle_interrupted(records, live, held, final_pass)` run through a defaulted `Steps::settle_interrupted` hook before the queue view and after the sweep. It closes originals whose retry ended and reports every dispatched job still without an outcome as held with a reason. `status` already lists every dispatched job without a process; its only change is that a job whose lock another process holds shows as running, not interrupted. The six live jobs get operator commands against the live records, outside the diff.

decisions.choice: Define 'no process' as `!running(job) && !job_lock_held(job)`, through a new `Athena::in_flight(&self, job:&str)->bool` in status.rs next to `running`. Pass `|j| athena.in_flight(j)` to `interrupted_work`, `settle_interrupted`, and `state_name` in status. Do not change `Athena::running`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. `running` checks only registry entries (status.rs:885-887), which are per agent process group, but `go_job` holds the job lock (`try_lock_job`, run/mod.rs:443) for the whole of `dispatch`, including planning gaps, preflight and CI waits. `Athena::retry` does not take the original's lock, so dropping the channel filter on a registry-only test could make the drain duplicate a live job of another consumer. The codebase already treats the free lock as the liveness signal (drain.rs `reclaim_interrupted` doc; disk.rs:188,233) and `StateDir::job_lock_held` (state.rs:153) is a probe that never creates a lock file. In a parallel drain the workers' own locks are held by other file handles, so they read as live too.

rejected.option: Change `Athena::running` itself to include the lock probe
rejected.why: `go_job` holds the job's own lock and then calls `self.running(id)` (run/mod.rs:478) to tell 'running' from 'was interrupted'; `resume_seed` and `earlier_attempt_with` also call it. It would misreport the job's own lock and change messages that tests pin.

rejected.option: Registry-only test with the channel filter removed (previous plan)
rejected.why: Retries a live off-channel job and calls it 'not worked' (finding 4).
Leaves off-channel dispatched jobs with no outcome forever, the reported fault.

decisions.choice: Close a job whose run errors after the Dispatch commit, inside `dispatch`, as `failed` with reason `stopped by an error after dispatch, before the job closed: <redacted error>`, via the existing `close_dispatched` with a `Closing` whose `new_invocations` come from the new `recover_traces` (completed live invocation records plus partial-usage files only).
decisions.reason: This is where the fault starts: `finish_dispatched` calls `close_dispatched` only on Ok (run/mod.rs:1342-1345). `failed` follows `stop_planning` (planning.rs:8-14), which ends a job that stopped before the producer as failed; a failed job can be retried (retry.rs:38-47), an abandoned one cannot. `dispatch` holds the job lock, so `Athena::close` (manage.rs:96) cannot be called from there; `close_dispatched` can.

rejected.why: Closes as abandoned, which `earlier_attempt_with` refuses to retry (retry.rs:38-47).

rejected.option: Leave it dispatched and rely on the next drain
rejected.why: A deterministic error would leave a dispatched job with no outcome at every drain.

rejected.option: Close every Err including holds and stops
rejected.why: SlotWait, LowDisk, BudgetShort, the kill switch and a kept candidate are resumable; closing destroys work.

decisions.choice: Split `Athena::recover_interrupted` (manage.rs:240-310) into `recover_traces(job) -> (Vec<NewFile>, Vec<Invocation>)` (live records and partial-usage files, lines 245-279) and the existing synthesis of a `Missing` producer (lines 280-307). `recover_interrupted` calls both, so `athena close` behaves exactly as today. The error close in `dispatch` calls only `recover_traces`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 5. The synthesis (manage.rs:285-306) books a producer at the full producer cap because a dead process leaves no trace. In `dispatch` the process is alive and knows what ran; an error before the producer spawns (for example `producer_snapshot`, producer.rs:125-146) must not book a phantom producer. Keeping the in-flight `Closing` reachable is not possible without changing the by-value signature of `produce_and_verify` (run/mod.rs:1738), which would widen the change; the state-directory traces hold the same invocations (each is mirrored by `invoke_and_record` before it returns, invocation.rs:257-261).

rejected.why: Changes the signature of the producer and verifier path, which this job must not touch.
A boolean parameter hides two behaviors; two named functions are clearer.

decisions.choice: The error-close guard: skip (return the original Err) when the error downcasts to LowDisk, SlotWait or BudgetShort, when `state.registry().stopped()`, or when `state.read_resume(id)` is Some. Only the post-commit section is wrapped; pre-commit errors are untouched.
decisions.reason: Keeps every deliberate hold and resumable job as a hold and leaves 'nothing committed' errors alone (run_pin_tests.rs:350-363, 695-716).

rejected.option: Close on any error whose job has no candidate
rejected.why: A kill-switch stop mid-planning has no candidate but is a stop, not a failure.

decisions.choice: Bound on repeated failed retries (answers finding 6): rely on the existing bounds and prove them with a test. An item gets `ATTEMPTS = 2` attempts per drain (drain.rs:284, 1942-1955); a closed failed job is not listed by `RealSteps::queue` (`queued_work` lists only Queued/Proposed, `interrupted_work` only Dispatched), so a later drain does not re-queue it; the scope guard pauses a line after repeated failures (`paused_reason`, drain.rs:1875, 1948); `earlier_jobs` caps a chain at `MAX_RETRY_DEPTH = 16` (retry.rs:583).
decisions.reason: No new counter is needed: the error close produces an ordinary failed job, which the drain already handles. The drain test asserts that after the first drain the request has at most two failed jobs and that a second drain dispatches no new job.

rejected.why: Duplicates ATTEMPTS and the scope guard; more state for no gain.

decisions.choice: Drop the channel filter in `interrupted_work` only, and exclude jobs for which `reading::retries_by_job` has a standing retry; keep `DRAINED_CHANNELS` in `queued_work` (steward.rs:414). Liveness comes from the `live` closure of decision 1.
decisions.reason: A queued request on another channel may belong to another consumer; a dispatched job with neither a registry entry nor a held lock belongs to nobody. Using `retries_by_job` gives drain the definition status already uses (status.rs:913), so a dropped retry no longer hides the original.

rejected.why: Changes unrelated queued-request behavior.

rejected.option: Keep the filter and close off-channel jobs
rejected.why: Discards resumable work.

decisions.choice: New pure `steward::settle_interrupted(records, live, held, final_pass) -> Vec<Settlement>` (`Close{job,why}` / `Hold{job,why}`), reached through a defaulted `Steps::settle_interrupted(&self, final_pass: bool) -> Vec<String>`. `RealSteps` implements it with `Athena::close`. Population: `records.request_jobs()` in state Dispatched with `!live(job)`. Rules: (1) `held(job)` is Some (disk or slot marker, `disk::read_any_hold`, run/mod.rs:481-490): Hold, never Close. (2) No request record (`athena retry` refuses it, retry.rs:54-56): Close, reason 'dispatched with no request record; it cannot be retried'. (3) A standing retry (`retries_by_job`), followed through interrupted retries to depth 16: last retry closed -> Close every interrupted job of the chain with `re-queued as <retry>, which ended <state>`; open -> Hold 'retried as <retry>, still <state>'. (4) No standing retry and `final_pass == false`: nothing (the drain is about to retry it). (5) No standing retry and `final_pass == true`: Hold 'dispatched with no outcome and no process; not worked in this drain (job limit, budget, stop, or its retry could not be read); `athena retry <job>` resumes it, `athena close <job> --why ...` closes it'.
decisions.reason: A pure function over `Records` is unit-tested without a model; a defaulted trait method leaves every test stub unedited, as `reclaim_interrupted` does (drain.rs:576). `Athena::close` recovers invocations, cleans and commits under the gate, and takes the job lock, so a live job is refused even if the liveness probe raced.

rejected.why: `queue()` also serves `athena plan`, which must stay read-only.
Forces edits to every stub.

rejected.option: Close every dispatched job without a standing retry at the end of the drain
rejected.why: Discards resumable work; resuming comes first.
Touches athena-data, the gate and round-trip tests for no gain.

decisions.reason: One constant, so hestia's text and steward's cannot drift; no behavior change. The error close is a `failed` outcome, which `closed_by_person` (hestia.rs:346-356) does not match.

risks.risk: The error close ends a job as failed that a later drain would have resumed, for example after a transient fault.
risks.mitigation: Only errors with no hold type, no kill switch and no kept candidate (resume mark absent) are closed. The outcome is `failed`, so `athena retry` and the drain's second attempt can run it again from the request. A hold or a built candidate stays dispatched.

risks.risk: An infrastructure error counts as a failed job in introspection and the scope guard and could pause a line after repeated errors.
risks.mitigation: This matches the `stop_planning` precedent (planning.rs:8-14). The reason has a fixed prefix so a person can tell it from a verifier failure. Raised in open_questions.

risks.risk: Repeated failed retries of a request whose run errors the same way every time (finding 6).
risks.mitigation: Existing bounds: ATTEMPTS = 2 per item per drain (drain.rs:284, 1942), no re-listing of a closed failed job by `queue`, the scope guard pause, and `MAX_RETRY_DEPTH` 16. The error-after-dispatch drain test asserts at most two failed jobs after the first drain and no new job from a second drain.

risks.risk: The drain retries or closes a live job another process runs (finding 4).
risks.mitigation: `Athena::in_flight` checks the registry and the job lock; it feeds the queue view, the settle and status. The settle's close goes through `Athena::close`, which takes the lock itself. A real-steps test holds the lock of an off-channel dispatched job with no registry entry and asserts it is neither retried, closed, nor named in a held line. A race between the probe and a retry is small and the retry's own dispatch takes a new job's lock, as today for cli jobs.

risks.risk: The error close books a phantom producer invocation at the producer cap (finding 5).
risks.mitigation: The error close uses `recover_traces` only (completed live records and partial-usage files). `recover_interrupted`, with the synthesis, stays for `athena close`. A unit test shows a job with no traces yields no invocation from `recover_traces`, and the planning-off error test finds no Missing producer. An invocation that completed but whose live-record write failed is recovered from its partial-usage file as a cap-bounded record; that over-states cost, never under-states it.

risks.risk: The reason text of the error may carry a secret or a machine path.
risks.mitigation: The reason goes through `ctx.redactor.redact` before it is committed; if redaction fails, a fixed text without the error is used. A test puts a path in the error.

risks.risk: `close_dispatched` itself fails, so the job stays dispatched.
risks.mitigation: The original error is returned with the second error as context, as today. The next drain lists the job and the final-pass settle reports it with a reason.

risks.risk: Closing an original too early could lose work or retry it twice.
risks.mitigation: Settle closes only when the standing retry (followed through interrupted retries) has an outcome; an open retry gives a Hold note; a held job is never closed. Unit tests cover running, lock-held, held, open, closed and chained cases; a drain test asserts the retried original is not retried twice.

risks.risk: `retries_by_job` treats an abandoned retry as not standing, so closing a middle job could re-list its parent for a second retry.
risks.mitigation: The settle follows the chain and closes every interrupted job in it in one pass, with a depth cap of 16. A Z-A-B unit test covers it.

risks.risk: Resuming off-channel jobs reverses a documented rule and an existing test.
risks.mitigation: The rewrite is explicit and named in the CHANGELOG. `queued_work` keeps its filter, pinned by a new test. The change applies only to dispatched jobs with no registry entry and no held lock.

risks.risk: Closing during a parallel drain races with a worker.
risks.mitigation: Settle errors become notes and never fail the drain. `close` takes the job lock and refuses a job another process runs. The final call comes after `sweep`, when all workers have finished.

risks.risk: The `interrupt` helper leaves the history one commit short, unlike a real process death.
risks.mitigation: It is used only for the restart shape. The error-path tests use the real code path (blocked live dir). Each test asserts before the drain that the job has no invocation and no outcome. `go_with_disk` (tests/drain.rs:2424) covers the hold case.

risks.risk: The six outcomes cannot be written by the diff because records/ is excluded.
risks.mitigation: The diff holds code, tests and CHANGELOG only. Demonstration 4 is an operator step after merge, with each close citing a hash read from git log. It needs write access to the live records.

risks.risk: Settle's `Athena::close` books a Missing producer at the cap for an original that never ran a producer (existing `athena close` behavior).
risks.mitigation: This is what a person's `athena close` does today and keeps the cost bound honest for a dead process; the settle does not alter it. Noted in the CHANGELOG entry.

demonstrations.method: Four layers, each stopping a dispatched job before the producer runs and driving a production entry point. (1) Core: `Athena::go` with `repo_with_planning(1)`; the planning script plants the blocking `records` file at Role::Planner so the first invocation fails after the Dispatch commit; plus a planning-off case where the error is raised before the spawn (unit test of `recover_traces` on a job directory with no traces: returns nothing, and `recover_interrupted` still synthesizes the Missing producer for `athena close`). (2) Drain, real steps: a cli job and a web job stopped with `interrupt`, then `drain::drain`; and a job whose producer-role script fails after dispatch. (3) A job whose lock is held with no registry entry. (4) steward `settle_*` unit tests.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core run::tests::an_error_after_dispatch && cargo test --locked -p athena-core manage::tests::recover_traces && cargo test --locked -p athena-core steward::tests && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain -- interrupted
demonstrations.observes: Core: `go` returns Finished with state Failed and a reason starting `stopped by an error after dispatch`; the job has job.json and brief-producer.md, a recovered planner invocation and no producer invocation (no phantom Missing producer); a low-disk hold and a kill-switch stop are left Dispatched. Drain: both interrupted originals (cli and web) end Closed(Abandoned) with a reason starting `re-queued as <retry>`; the error-after-dispatch job ends Closed(Failed) in the same drain with the failure reason in the report; after the first drain the request has at most two failed jobs and a second drain dispatches no new job (bound of finding 6: ATTEMPTS, drain.rs:284). The job whose lock is held is not retried, no `held <job>` note names it and it stays Dispatched. Steward: held job is Hold, request-less job is Close, open retry is Hold, closed retry is Close, dropped retry gives no settle but is listed by `interrupted_work`, running or lock-held job gives nothing, chain Z-A-B closes both, `final_pass` false gives nothing and true gives a Hold with a reason.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the dispatch wrapper `go` returns Err and the job stays dispatched with no outcome, so the core and drain error tests fail. Without the new `interrupted_work`, the web job is not listed and stays dispatched; a job whose retry was dropped is never re-listed; a job whose retry landed stays dispatched. Without the lock probe the live off-channel job is retried and the lock test fails. With `recover_interrupted` used on the error path the planning-off test finds a phantom producer.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `Athena::go` (run/mod.rs:402) and `drain::drain(&steps, limits(100.0), &Quiet)` with `RealSteps` from `real_steps(&athena, &lander)` (tests/drain.rs:4365, exists). Fixtures that exist: `athena_with`, `repo_with_planning`, `planning_script` (run/tests.rs:187, 287, 1189), `Fixture::new()`, `killing_producer`, `interrupt`, `request_on` (tests/drain.rs:5094, 5108, 4968), the steward `add` helper (steward.rs:2118-2216), `StateDir::try_lock_job`. Doubles: scripted agent and `RecordingLander` only; the error close, listing, settle and lock probe are production code. Steps that add production seams: the dispatch wrapper and `recover_traces`; `Athena::in_flight`; `steward::settle_interrupted`; the `Steps` hook.

open_questions: User: May a job that was interrupted and whose standing retry ended rejected or failed be closed as abandoned with the reason `re-queued as <retry>, which ended <state>`? The plan does so, because the retry carries the work forward and the original would otherwise stay dispatched for ever. The alternative is to leave it listed as 'retried as X' until a person closes it.

User: Should an error after dispatch with no kept candidate close the job as `failed` (retryable, counted by introspection and the scope guard, as `stop_planning` does) or as `abandoned` (not counted, but `athena retry` refuses it)? The plan uses `failed`.

Host: Which of the six jobs' work already landed through another job, and which commit hashes should be cited? The live job records and full git log are not in the snapshot. HISTORY.txt shows 5874b1f (Transport row to gh/transport.rs) and 612c27f (run.rs to run/mod.rs), both 2026-10-27, as candidates only; 77zh, w1y3 and z7sj are not identified by any evidence in the snapshot.

Host: What error or process death left each of the six jobs without an outcome, and what channel and retry history do they have? The records and logs are absent from the snapshot, so which origin applied to each is not shown by the code; the plan fixes both origins and tests each.
